cfp.format: 12 teams: 5 automatic bids + 7 at-large. Automatic: the champions of the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC, plus the highest-ranked champion of the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12 and Sun Belt. Notre Dame is in if it finishes in the top 12 of the final ranking. An automatic qualifier ranked outside the top 12 still gets in and takes one of the lowest seeds.
cfp.seeding: Straight seeding from the committee's final ranking (approved May 2025); seeds 1–4 receive first-round byes whether or not they are conference champions. First round on the higher seed's campus: 12 at 5, 11 at 6, 10 at 7, 9 at 8. Quarterfinals: 1 v 8/9, 2 v 7/10, 3 v 6/11, 4 v 5/12. No reseeding; no adjustment for rematches or conference opponents. From 2026 the No. 1 seed picks its quarterfinal bowl and semifinal site, then No. 2, No. 3; No. 4 gets the remaining bowl.
cfp.source: College Football Playoff Management Committee vote 2026-01-23 (as summarised by National Football Post, 2026-10-23); FBSchedules
cfp.expansion: A 24-team format for 2027 is under discussion (ESPN report 2026-10-15) and is NOT approved; any 2027 change must be decided by Dec 1, 2026. Until the CFP announces one, the 12-team format is the only confirmed format.

rules_used_by_the_model.conference_title_games: Every conference but the Independents plays one; the two teams with the best conference record meet (Sun Belt: the East and West division winners). The Pac-12's Week 13 flex game counts as non-conference.
rules_used_by_the_model.tiebreakers: Each conference's published tiebreakers are long (head-to-head, common opponents, then ratings composites). The HOUSE MODEL applies conference win percentage, then head-to-head between two tied teams, then its own rating — an approximation, labelled as such.
rules_used_by_the_model.bowl_eligibility: Six wins (at most one against an FCS opponent counts) — the HOUSE MODEL's 'bowl eligible' line; the NCAA's waiver and APR backfill rules are not modelled.
